an3.20:2.1: _Vidhura_ is rare and its meaning inconsistent in the commentaries. At [snp5.1:21.3]() it is glossed _vigatadhuro_ (“free of burden”, followed by Norman) and _appaṭimo_ (“unrivalled”, followed by Bodhi), whereas the same word here is glossed “of distinguished burden, endowed with energy connected with knowledge” (followed by Bodhi’s “responsible”). But the Jātakas know Vidhura as a wise adviser to the Kuru kings Yudhiṭṭhila ([ja413]()) and Dhanañjaya ([ja548]()). This must be the same person remembered in the Mahābhārata as Vidura, brother and wise adviser to the Kuru king Dhṛtarāṣṭra, uncle of Yudhiṣṭhira and Dhanañjaya AKA Arjuna. Hence we should accept _vidhura_ as the Pali spelling of Sanskrit _vidura_, from the root _vid_ (“knowing”), so I render as “acumen”.
an3.20:3.5: Even a talented entrepreneur, it seems, can only flourish with the help of others.
